title: Implement Resilient Pipeline State Checkpointing and Recovery
description: The PulseStream Insight Engine is a high-performance data analytics platform that processes continuous data streams. A critical weakness is its lack of fault tolerance; if the engine crashes or is restarted, the state of all in-flight processing pipelines is lost, leading to data loss and requiring full reprocessing. This task involves implementing a robust checkpointing mechanism to periodically save the state of active pipelines to disk, allowing the engine to resume from the last known good state upon restart.

project_spec.name: PulseStream Insight Engine
project_spec.description:
PulseStream Insight Engine is an end-to-end healthcare analytics hub designed as a single, self-contained C application that ingests high-frequency physiological signals (e.g., ECG, SpO₂), EHR snapshots, and HL7/FHIR event streams from hospital wards, then cleanses, enriches, analyzes, and visualizes them for clinicians and quality-assurance teams. Operating as a monolith, it embeds an internal ETL Pipeline that lands raw data in an on-disk Data Lake, triggers configurable Strategy-Pattern-based transformation chains (e.g., ICU-specific vs. ambulatory rules), and emits near-real-time dashboards as well as governed research extracts. 

The engine features an internal Scheduler for timed batch loads, a Stream Processing core that parallelizes windowed analytics across CPU cores (POSIX threads + SIMD), and a robust Observer Pattern that propagates state changes—such as new device connections or anomaly detections—through the system for alerting and automated error recovery. Built-in data-quality checks flag missing vitals or malformed HL7 segments, while a monitoring subsystem records performance counters and health metrics to ensure regulatory-grade auditability. A native OpenGL overlay renders ICU trend lines, cohort heatmaps, and predictive risk scores directly from the monolith, eliminating external BI dependencies yet allowing the deployment team to ship a single binary to on-prem clinical data centers.

This design deliberately avoids runtime service orchestration overhead, instead packaging 60 tightly-coupled modules (files) that compile into one executable (~297k tokens of source) suited for locked-down hospital environments where inter-process communication and network exposure are heavily restricted.
dependencies: HDF5 C API (columnar Data Lake file format for high-frequency signals)
libcurl (secure HTTPS ingestion from FHIR/HL7 endpoints)
czmq (ZeroMQ C bindings for in-process publish/subscribe Observer Pattern)
OpenMP (parallel for loops in transformation and analytics stages)
OpenBLAS (vectorized numerical routines for risk-score algorithms)
libuv (event loop & high-resolution timers for scheduler/stream engine)
spdlog (file & syslog logging with rotation for audit trail)
